# Fluence window probe

This standalone, opt-in diagnostic runs outside the solution, package, and unit CI. Build `Fluence.WindowProbe.csproj` for `net472`, `net8.0-windows10.0.26100.0`, or `net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0` and run a fresh process for each observation.

```powershell
dotnet run --project tools/Fluence.WindowProbe/Fluence.WindowProbe.csproj --framework net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0 -- --mode fluence --theme Dark --backdrop Mica --render-mode default --size fixed --output C:\Temp\fluence-probe.ndjson
```

`--mode` is `plain`, `chrome-dwm`, `fluence`, or `wpf-fluent`. The last mode requires .NET 10 and uses WPF's documented Fluent resources and `Window.ThemeMode`. `plain` and `wpf-fluent` do not accept `--backdrop`; their requested backdrop is `N/A`. The material modes accept `None`, `Mica`, `Acrylic`, or `Tabbed`, defaulting to `Mica`. `--theme` is `Light` or `Dark` (default `Light`), `--render-mode` is `default` or `software-only` (default `default`), `--size` is `fixed` or `content` (default `fixed`), `--topmost` is `on` or `off` (default `off`), and `--output` must be an absolute path. `--help` prints usage. `--auto-close-ms N` closes the window after `Loaded` for unattended diagnostics; omit it for manual inspection. Use `--topmost on` only for a controlled capture when foreground applications otherwise occlude the probe. It changes z-order and does not prove ordinary activation behavior.

Fixed mode requests 640×440 WPF units at (80,80) in WPF coordinates. The probe manifest requests Per Monitor V2 DPI awareness, with a Per Monitor fallback; inspect each record's actual DPI and physical `GetWindowRect` coordinates before choosing a capture region. Content mode sizes to the live content and grows when a row is added.

Only `chrome-dwm` accepts `--explicit-target-clear on|off`, `--full-glass on|off`, `--dwm-attribute on|off`, and `--force-target-opaque on|off`. Their defaults are `on`, `on`, `on`, and `off`. The force option overwrites the target after chrome initialization for a diagnostic contrast. Disabling the explicit clear skips the probe-owned initial clear, though `WindowChrome` may still clear the target; subsequent theme/backdrop actions synchronize the target with the selected material. Active material uses a transparent WPF window background; `None`, a disabled DWM setter, or a failed setter uses a solid theme fallback. The WPF Fluent mode leaves its window background to WPF's Fluent policy.

Buttons cycle Light/Dark, cycle Mica/Acrylic/Tabbed/None where applicable, and add a named content row in content-size mode. Inapplicable buttons are disabled; `NextBackdrop` is disabled when the probe's DWM setter is off. `NextTheme`, `NextBackdrop`, and `GrowContent` are their UI Automation IDs. Every action writes before and after records. Enter and exit OS High Contrast manually; each record includes the observed state.

The custom Chrome mode reserves a 48-DIP title area and uses a 4-DIP resize border. Fluence supplies its own title area. Native-caption modes use a metric-based spacer to keep the interior content near the same screen origin; the record includes the measured physical content origin and title-area description. On the 150% DPI smoke host, content origins span 156-167 physical X pixels and 228-234 physical Y pixels despite identical outer bounds. Native and custom caption controls still differ. The comparison should use a common interior crop as well as a full-window capture.

The NDJSON records distinguish requested state from WPF capability and native readback. `RenderCapabilityTier` is the raw WPF value and `RenderCapabilityTierLevel` is its upper-word tier; neither establishes the selected render backend. A failed DWM query has its HRESULT, a null value, and a failure status. HWND style has a separate Win32 status/error, and direct dark-mode setter attempts retain both primary and fallback HRESULTs. Fluence's internal native call results are unobserved. `SourceInitialized-event` is the public event callback; for `FluenceWindow` it occurs during base source initialization before its later backdrop setup. `after-Show` is a separate snapshot. The first WPF rendering callback and `ContentRendered` are timing clues, not a first DWM present.

For first-frame evidence, start an external compositor recording before `Show` and capture a fixed, known, unoccluded window region including its border. Record frame rate, dropped frames, and sampling gaps. On RDP, capture client-delivered pixels as well as the server-side trace. A `RenderTargetBitmap` or settled `PrintWindow` capture cannot prove the first visible frame.
